answer: The tundra cap is upheld at intake and anchor makes public the per-origin counts. At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a karst tag. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a fleet in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, since each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
